days.label: Rig Veda 1.1 to 1.12
days.key: I laud Agni, the chosen Priest, God, minister of sacrifice, The Hotar, lavishest of wealth.
days.s: The collection opens with the singer praising the fire god through his offices at the rite; Sāyaṇa, on 1.1.1, explains ‘chosen Priest’ first by a likeness: Agni accomplishes the offering the sacrifice requires as a king’s household priest accomplishes what the king desires.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.1.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 410218 (2025)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.13 to 1.23
days.key: Through all this world strode Visnu; thrice his foot he planted, and the whole Was gathered in his footstep’s dust.
days.s: In a hymn to many gods, six closing verses sing of Visnu and his strides; Yāska, Nirukta 12.19, explains the three steps by two teachers’ views: on earth, mid-air and heaven, or on the mountain of sunrise, the meridian and the mountain of sunset.
days.src: Yāska, Nirukta 12.19, trans. Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta (1920 to 1921), archive.org nighantuniruktao00yask

days.label: Rig Veda 1.24 to 1.30
days.key: WHATEVER law of thine, O God, O Varuna, as we are men, Day after day we violate.
days.s: Pleading with Varuna not to strike in anger, the hymn opens with an admission; Sāyaṇa, on 1.25.1, takes the law as the rite, which the worshippers, careless as subjects at times are, damage day by day, and supplies a prayer that Varuna make it whole.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.25.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 283258 (2020)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.31 to 1.35
days.key: I will declare the manly deeds of Indra, the first that he achieved, the Thunder-wielder. He slew the Dragon, then disclosed the waters, and cleft the channels of the mountain torrents.
days.s: Opening a hymn on Indra’s fight with Vrtra, the singer announces the god’s first deeds; Sāyaṇa, on 1.32.1, takes ‘the Dragon’ as the cloud and counts three deeds: slaying the cloud, bringing the waters down to earth, and setting the mountain rivers flowing.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.32.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 403053 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.36 to 1.44
days.key: Let him not love to speak ill words: but fear the One who holds all four Within his hand, until they fall.
days.s: A hymn on those the Adityas guard ends with a warning about speech; Sāyaṇa, on 1.41.9, takes the four as cowrie shells in a game of dice, their holder feared by the other player until they fall, as evil speech should be feared.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.41.9, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 350337 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.45 to 1.51
days.key: Looking upon the loftier light above the darkness we have come To Surya, God among the Gods, the light that is most excellent.
days.s: In a hymn to the rising Sun, just before a prayer for healing, the worshippers tell of their coming; Sāyaṇa, on 1.50.10, takes the darkness as night or as sin, and the coming as union with the Sun, since people become what they worship.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.50.10, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 401983 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.52 to 1.58
days.key: In fear they raised the lofty self-resplendent hymn, praise giving and effectual, leading up to heaven, When Indra’s helpers fighting for the good of men, the Maruts, faithful to mankind, joyed in the light.
days.s: Between Vrtra’s fall and Heaven reeling in terror at the Dragon’s roar, the hymn remembers the battle; Sāyaṇa, on 1.52.9, reads the ‘lofty’ hymn as the Brhat Saman, sung in fear of Vrtra, and the Maruts as attending on men in the form of breath.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.52.9, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 237934 (2020)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.59 to 1.65
days.key: When Indra and the Angirases desired it, Sarama found provision for her offspring.
days.s: Praising Indra, by whom the Angirases found the cattle, the hymn tells of the search; Sāyaṇa, on 1.62.3, reads it through the tale of Sarama, the gods’ hound, sent after the cows the Panis stole, going only once Indra promised their milk to her young.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.62.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 400586 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.66 to 1.77
days.key: Soon as the holy beings had discovered the thrice-seven mystic things contained within thee, With these, one-minded, they preserve the Amrta: guard thou the life of all their plants and cattle.
days.s: With Agni found in the loftiest station, the hymn speaks of what lies hidden in him; Sāyaṇa, on 1.72.6, reads the ‘thrice-seven’ as twenty-one sacrifices, seven each of cooked food, oblation and Soma, placed in Agni alone because no rite can be done without fire.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.72.6, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 220672 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.78 to 1.85
days.key: Then verily they recognized the essential form of Tvastar’s Bull, Here in the mansion of the Moon.
days.s: In a hymn to Indra, the verse follows the tale of Dadhyac’s bones and the horse’s head; Sāyaṇa, on 1.84.15, reads it as the sun’s rays recognising in the Moon’s clear watery orb their own light, hidden by night.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.84.15, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 400850 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.86 to 1.93
days.key: A hundred autumns stand before us, O ye Gods, within whose space ye bring our bodies to decay; Within whose space our sons become fathers in turn. Break ye not in the midst our course of fleeting life.
days.s: Having asked the Gods for firm limbs and the life they appoint, the hymn names that life’s length; Sāyaṇa, on 1.89.9, takes the hundred autumns as the span fixed for men at creation, and the sons as becoming their fathers’ guardians, or else fathers themselves.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.89.9, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 292662 (2020)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.94 to 1.101
days.key: Three several places of his birth they honour, in mid-air, in the heaven, and in the waters. Governing in the east of earthly regions, the seasons hath he stablished in their order.
days.s: In a hymn to Agni as a newborn infant, the verse counts his births; Sāyaṇa, on 1.95.3, reads the three as the fire beneath the ocean, the sun in heaven and the lightning, taking the first place as the sea and ‘the waters’ as mid-air.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.95.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 333253 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.102 to 1.108
days.key: That pathway of the Sun in heaven, made to be highly glorified, Is not to be transgressed, O Gods. O mortals, ye behold it not. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
days.s: In a lament that tells of Trita buried in a well, the singer points to the Sun’s road; Sāyaṇa, on 1.105.16, reads it as a road even the gods cannot overstep, since the seasons, the sacrifices and so the gods’ life depend on the Sun.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.105.16, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 400930 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.109 to 1.113
days.key: Gone are the men who in the days before us looked on the rising of the earlier Morning. We, we the living, now behold her brightness and they come nigh who shall hereafter see her.
days.s: In a hymn that follows Dawn through mornings past and to come, the singer counts the generations who see her; Sāyaṇa, on 1.113.11, reads the verse as meaning that Dawn pervades all three times, past, present and future.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.113.11, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 401270 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.114 to 1.117
days.key: The soul of all that moveth not or moveth, the Sun hath filled the air and earth and heaven.
days.s: A hymn to the Sun opens on his rising and follows his horses to nightfall; Sāyaṇa, on 1.115.1, reads the Sun first as the supreme Self moving all from within, the cause from which the moving and unmoving world is not separate.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.115.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 329056 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.118 to 1.123
days.key: Fain to bring light to homes of men the noble and active Goddess hath emerged from darkness.
days.s: A hymn to Dawn opens with the Daksina’s broad chariot harnessed and the immortal Gods aboard; Sāyaṇa, on 1.123.1, reads the Goddess’s purpose as healing, a cure she works on the dwellings of men by driving away the darkness of night.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.123.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 348392 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.124 to 1.129
days.key: Not interrupting heavenly ordinances, although she minisheth human generations. The last of endless morns that have departed, the first of those that come, Dawn brightly shineth.
days.s: As the fire is kindled and Savitar sends all creatures to work, the hymn weighs Dawn’s dealings with Gods and men; Sāyaṇa, on 1.124.2, reads her as helping the Gods’ rites like the Agnihotra with her light while wearing away the life of men.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.124.2, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 368324 (2023)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.130 to 1.135
days.key: Couples desirous of thine aid are storming thee, pouring their presents forth to win a stall of kine, pouring gifts, Indra, seeking thee.
days.s: With Heaven and Earth bowed to Indra, the hymn tells of those who worship him; Sāyaṇa, on 1.131.3, reads the ‘couples’ as husbands and wives, holding that a wife may share the rite with her husband, though not perform it alone.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.131.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 207804 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.136 to 1.142
days.key: Grant to our chariot, to our house, O Agni, a boat with moving feet and constant oarage, One that may further well our wealthy princes and all the folk, and be our certain refuge.
days.s: After following Agni’s flames through plants and trees, the hymn closes on prayers for gifts; Sāyaṇa, on 1.140.12, reads the boat as the Soma sacrifice, its oars the priests, its feet the offerings, gods and mantras, carrying sacrificers across the round of birth and death.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.140.12, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 401272 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.143 to 1.154
days.key: May I attain to that his well-loved mansion where men devoted to the Gods are happy. For there springs, close akin to the Wide-Strider, the well of meath in Visnu’s highest footstep.
days.s: After praising Visnu’s three strides across the worlds, the singer voices his own longing; Sāyaṇa, on 1.154.5, takes the mansion as the imperishable world of Brahman, free of hunger, thirst, old age, death and return, and Visnu as kin to all who do good.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.154.5, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 403472 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.155 to 1.162
days.key: No, here thou diest not, thou art not injured: by easy paths unto the Gods thou goest.
days.s: Near the end of a hymn on the horse sacrifice, the horse, now killed, is addressed; Sāyaṇa, on 1.162.21, takes the killing as no death like other horses’ and no pointless harm, answering the objection that the death is seen: the horse reaches the gods.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.162.21, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 401046 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.163 to 1.164
days.key: They call him Indra, Mitra, Varuna, Agni, and he is heavenly nobly-winged Garutman. To what is One, sages give many a title they call it Agni, Yama, Matarisvan.
days.s: Just after a riddle on the four divisions of speech, in a long hymn of riddles, the singer runs through the names of the gods; Sāyaṇa, on 1.164.46, reads the One as the Sun, not other than Brahman and so the self of all, and Yāska, Nirukta 7.18, as this very Agni, the great self.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.164.46, sa.wikisource, revision 402071 (2024); Yāska, Nirukta 7.18, trans. Lakshman Sarup (1920 to 1921)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.165 to 1.171
days.key: NAUGHT is to-day, to-morrow naught. Who comprehends the mystery? We must address ourselves unto another’s thought, and lost is then the hope we formed.
days.s: A short hymn of quarrel over an offering, naming Indra, Agastya and the Maruts, opens with a complaint; Sāyaṇa, on 1.170.1, hears Indra lamenting an offering set aside for him and given to another, and giving up hope of it today or tomorrow.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.170.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 207936 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.172 to 1.182
days.key: Here sprung to life, they both have sung together, with bodies free from stain, with signs that mark them; One of you Prince of Sacrifice, the Victor, the other counts as Heaven’s auspicious offspring.
days.s: Between prayers for the Asvins’ car and steeds, the hymn sets the twins side by side; Sāyaṇa, on 1.181.4, reads them as the Moon, son of mid-air, whose rising makes plants grow, and the Sun, son of heaven, each upholding the world.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.181.4, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 207948 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 1.183 to 1.191
days.key: These of themselves support all things existing: as on a car the Day and Night roll onward.
days.s: Opening a hymn to Heaven and Earth, the singer asks which came first; Sāyaṇa, on 1.185.1, takes these lines as the reason none can know, since any cause one names is itself upheld by them, and, turning like wheels, they have no first.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.185.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 402616 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 2.1 to 2.8
days.key: Thee, Agni, have the Adityas taken as their mouth; the Bright Ones have made thee, O Sage, to be their tongue. They who love offerings cling to thee at solemn rites: by thee the Gods devour the duly offered food.
days.s: In the book’s opening hymn, which names Agni as each god in turn, the verse speaks of the gods; Sāyaṇa, on 2.1.13, reads them as eating and tasting only through Agni, waiting on him since without him they cannot eat the oblation.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.1.13, Sanskrit text at sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 400202 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 2.9 to 2.14
days.key: Of whom, the Terrible, they ask, Where is He? or verily they say of him, He is not. He sweeps away, like birds, the foe’s possessions. Have faith in him, for He, O men, is Indra.
days.s: In a hymn whose refrain names Indra to the people, this verse meets those who doubt him; Sāyaṇa, on 2.12.5, reads the doubters as those who, not seeing him, think him nowhere, and the verse as bidding trust that Indra is, though not plainly seen.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.12.5, Sanskrit text at sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 401594 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 2.15 to 2.22
days.key: THE rich new car hath been equipped at morning; four yokes it hath, three whips, seven reins to guide it: Ten-sided, friendly to mankind, light-winner, that must be urged to speed with prayers and wishes.
days.s: Opening a hymn that calls Indra to the Soma with ever more horses, the verse pictures a car; Sāyaṇa, on 2.18.1, first reads the car as the morning sacrifice, its yokes the pressing-stones, its whips three pitches of voice, its reins the seven metres.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.18.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 208756 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 2.23 to 2.28
days.key: Move far from me what sins I have committed: let me not suffer, King, for guilt of others. Full many a morn remains to dawn upon us: in these, O Varuna, while we live direct us.
days.s: Late in a hymn to Varuna, the verse follows praise of his unmoving statutes; Sāyaṇa, on 2.28.8, reads the sins as debts, the singer’s forebears’ and his own, and the undawned mornings as dawns that seem not to break for a debtor awake before daylight.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.28.8 (his verse 9), sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 208788 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 2.29 to 2.34
days.key: What time hath past since they were first set flowing?
days.s: Opening a hymn chiefly to Indra, the verse tells of waters that never rest from flowing; Sāyaṇa, on 2.30.1, takes the question as a dismissal, since the waters are eternal and there was no first time to measure.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.30.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 213335 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 2.35 to 2.41
days.key: What was spread out she weaves afresh, re-weaving: the skillful leaves his labour half-completed.
days.s: In a hymn to Savitar, the verse comes just after Night is said to follow his rule; Sāyaṇa, on 2.38.4, reads the weaver as Night, who like a woman weaving cloth wraps up again the light that lay spread out.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.38.4, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 222990 (2020)

days.label: Rig Veda 2.42 to 3.4
days.key: They who are free from death, fain for him, purified three splendours of the mighty Agni, circling all. To man, for his enjoyment, one of these they gave: the other two have passed into the sister sphere.
days.s: Hailing Agni as Vaisvanara, High Priest of the Gods, the hymn praises his threefold fire; Sāyaṇa, on 3.2.9, reads the three as his earthly, lightning and solar forms, the earthly one set among mortals, or else as the rite’s three fuel sticks.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 3.2.9, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 315134 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 3.5 to 3.13
days.key: Three times a hundred Gods and thrice a thousand, and three times ten and nine have worshipped Agni, For him spread sacred grass, with oil bedewed him, and stablished him as Priest and Sacrificer.
days.s: Closing a hymn on Agni found hidden in the waters and fetched from afar by Matarisvan, the verse numbers the gods who served him; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 3.9.9, reads the count through the Bṛhadāraṇyaka, where the gods are thirty-three and the thousands only their powers.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 3.9.9, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 209084 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 3.14 to 3.26
days.key: Agni am I who know, by birth, all creatures. Mine eye is butter, in my mouth is nectar. I am light threefold, measurer of the region exhaustless heat am I, named burnt-oblation.
days.s: After the Kusikas call on Agni Vaisvanara and the storming Maruts, a voice speaks as Agni himself; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 3.26.7, reads it as Agni, who has seen the highest reality, declaring himself the self of all, eater and eaten, and so the supreme Brahman.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 3.26.7, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 402119 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 3.27 to 3.31
days.key: As Germ Celestial he is called Tanunapat, and Narasamsa born diffused in varied shape. Formed in his Mother he is Matarisvan; he hath, in his course, become the rapid flight of wind.
days.s: As the priests rub the fire-sticks and the flame is born, the hymn turns to the names Agni bears; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 3.29.11, reads them as stages: Tanunapat while an embryo in the sticks, Narasamsa once born, Matarisvan when he flashes in the mid-air.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 3.29.11, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 400415 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 3.32 to 3.37
days.key: Linger a little at my friendly bidding rest, Holy Ones, a moment in your journey. With hymn sublime soliciting your favour Kusika’s son hath called unto the River.
days.s: Answering the rivers, who ask what the singer wants of streams that cannot halt, the seer presses his request; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 3.33.5, takes the request as made for the Soma he will procure once across, and ‘the River’ as the Sutudri before him.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 3.33.5, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 360653 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 3.38 to 3.49
days.key: That day when thou wast born thou, fain to taste it, drankest the plant’s milk which the mountains nourish. That milk thy Mother first, the Dame who bare thee, poured for thee in thy mighty Father’s dwelling.
days.s: Early in a hymn on the newborn Indra’s thirst for Soma, the verse turns to his mother; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 3.48.2, takes her as Aditi and the dwelling as Kaśyapa’s birth-chamber, where she poured the Soma into his mouth before giving the breast.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 3.48.2, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 338677 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 3.50 to 3.54
days.key: What pathway leadeth to the Gods? Who knoweth this of a truth, and who will now declare it? Seen are their lowest dwelling-places only, but they are in remote and secret regions.
days.s: In praise of Heaven and Earth, the singer breaks off with questions; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 3.54.5, takes the visible seats as those of gods in the form of stars, and the way to seats won by hidden rites as known to none without the Veda.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 3.54.5, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 292777 (2020)

days.label: Rig Veda 3.55 to 3.62
days.key: May we attain that excellent glory of Savitar the God: So May he stimulate our prayers.
days.s: The book’s closing hymn is built of six triplets to different gods, and this verse begins Savitar’s; Sāyaṇa, on 3.62.10, first reads the glory as the self-luminous light that is the supreme Brahman, named for burning away ignorance, and the prayers as acts or understandings.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 3.62.10, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 330443 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 4.1 to 4.4
days.key: May he who knows distinguish sense and folly of men, like straight and crooked backs of horses.
days.s: After blessing each worshipper who brings Agni fuel, food or praise, the hymn turns to his judgement; Sāyaṇa, on 4.2.11, reads ‘sense and folly’ as merit and sin, or knowledge and ignorance, which Agni sorts as a groom sorts fit backs from unfit.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 4.2.11, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 403270 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 4.5 to 4.14
days.key: How is it that, unbound and not supported, he falleth not although directed downward? By what self power moves he? Who hath seen it?
days.s: In a hymn of sunrise that follows the Sun’s coursers up the sky, the closing verse turns to his motion; Sāyaṇa, on 4.13.5, reads ‘falleth not’ as saying the Sun, facing downward, is harmed by none, and the last question as meaning no one knows.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 4.13.5, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 209073 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 4.15 to 4.19
days.key: Not this way go I forth: hard is the passage. Forth from the side obliquely will I issue. Much that is yet undone must I accomplish; one must I combat and the other question.
days.s: The verse answers the first voice, which urges the old path of birth; Sāyaṇa, on 4.18.2, hears the sage Vāmadeva, still unborn, answering Indra, and takes the one to be fought as a rival, the one questioned as a seeker of knowledge.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 4.18.2, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 321007 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 4.20 to 4.26
days.key: I WAS aforetime Manu, I was Surya: I am the sage Kaksivan, holy singer. Kutsa the son of Arjuni I master. I am the sapient Usana behold me.
days.s: Before the hymn praises the Falcon who brought Soma, three verses speak in the first person; Sāyaṇa, on 4.26.1, hears in them Vāmadeva, still in the womb and knowing the truth, speak as the self of all and bid hearers know their own nature so.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 4.26.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 209120 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 4.27 to 4.34
days.key: This day have they set gladdening drink before you. Not without toil are Gods inclined to friendship.
days.s: The hymn on the Rbhus, whose labours made them immortal, ends at the third libation; Sāyaṇa, on 4.33.11, reads the toil as austerity, without which the gods befriend none, and takes the drink as given to the Rbhus because they had so toiled.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 4.33.11, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 401703 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 4.35 to 4.42
days.key: The Hamsa homed in light, the Vasu in mid-air, the priest beside the altar, in the house the guest, Dweller in noblest place, mid men, in truth, in sky, born of flood, kine, truth, mountain, he is holy Law.
days.s: The hymn to Dadhikravan ends by naming one being in his dwellings; Sāyaṇa, on 4.40.5, reads him as the Sun in heaven, wind in mid-air and fire at the altar, and the Sun as one with the Self in all creatures and with unconditioned Brahman.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 4.40.5, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 216198 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 4.43 to 4.53
days.key: Lighting all living creatures, ne’er to be deceived, Savitar, God, protects each holy ordinance. He hath stretched out his arms to all the folk of earth, and, with his laws observed, rules his own mighty course.
days.s: In a hymn that follows Savitar across heaven and earth, the verse turns to his care for all that lives; Sāyaṇa, on 4.53.4, reads the outstretched arms as his leave to each creature for its own work, since all activity depends on the Sun.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 4.53.4, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 222991 (2020)

days.label: Rig Veda 4.54 to 5.3
days.key: Four are his horns, three are the feet that bear him; his heads are two, his hands are seven in number. Bound with a triple bond the Steer roars loudly: the mighty God hath entered in to mortals.
days.s: In a hymn that praises the streams of holy oil poured to Agni, the verse turns to a many-limbed Steer; Sāyaṇa, on 4.58.3, reads it first as the sacrificial Agni: four Vedas for horns, three pressings for feet, seven metres for hands.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 4.58.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 402369 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 5.4 to 5.14
days.key: As I, remembering thee with grateful spirit, a mortal, call with might on thee Immortal, Vouchsafe us high renown, O Jatavedas, and may I be immortal by my children.
days.s: Near the end of a hymn that calls Agni father and guest, the singer makes his own plea; Sāyaṇa, on 5.4.10, reads this immortality as a line of descendants never broken, citing a text in which the mortal is born again in his offspring.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.4.10, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 324070 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 5.15 to 5.29
days.key: Show thyself strong for mighty bliss, O Agni, most excellent be thine effulgent splendours. Make easy to maintain our household lordship, and overcome the might of those who hate us.
days.s: In a short hymn of kindling and offering, after Agni is hailed as king, the prayer turns homeward; Sāyaṇa, on 5.28.3, reads ‘household lordship’ as the shared work of wife and husband, which Agni is to make well ordered, each bound to the other.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.28.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 199496 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 5.30 to 5.36
days.key: I have beheld his strong and secret dwelling, longing have sought the Founder’s habitation. I asked of others, and they said in answer, May we, awakened men, attain to Indra.
days.s: After asking who has seen Indra, the singer recounts his search; Sāyaṇa, on 5.30.2, takes him as a seer who asked whether Indra, though real, was hard to reach and, told he was not, saw the rest of the hymn for reaching Indra.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.30.2, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 398838 (2023)

days.label: Rig Veda 5.37 to 5.43
days.key: What time thou smotest down Svarbhanu’s magic that spread itself beneath the sky, O Indra, By his fourth sacred prayer Atri discovered Surya concealed in gloom that stayed his function.
days.s: As the hymn turns from Indra’s Soma to the Sun darkened by Svarbhanu, the verse tells how Atri freed the light; Sāyaṇa, on 5.40.6, takes the fourth prayer as the hymn’s eighth verse, each earlier one having driven off one part of the magic.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.40.5 and 5.40.6, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 403751 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 5.44 to 5.51
days.key: I seek for no release, no turning back therefrom. May he who knows the way, the Leader, guide me straight.
days.s: Opening a hymn to all the gods, the singer pictures himself yoked like a willing horse to a load; Sāyaṇa, on 5.46.1, takes the load as the sacrifice and the guide as the god who rules within, going before along its paths.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.46.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 199507 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 5.52 to 5.57
days.key: Bright shone your host, ye Sages, Maruts, when ye smote the waving tree as when the worm consumeth it. Accordant, as the eye guides him who walks, have ye led our devotion onward by an easy path.
days.s: In a hymn praising the Maruts for lightning and rain, the singer recalls their stroke and their guidance; Sāyaṇa, on 5.54.6, takes the tree as the rain cloud, named for being split, and the easy path as the singer’s road to wealth.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.54.6, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 403632 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 5.58 to 5.67
days.key: Yea, many a woman is more firm and better than the man who turns Away from Gods, and offers not.
days.s: In a hymn mixing praise of the Maruts with thanks to patrons, the verse follows a blessing on a woman; Sāyaṇa, on 5.61.6, takes her as Śaśīyasī, King Taranta’s queen, and the man as a miser who neither praises the gods nor gives.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.61 (introduction and verse 6), sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 403490 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 5.68 to 5.81
days.key: Worship at dawn and instigate the Asvins: nor is the worshipper at eve rejected. Besides ourselves another craves and worships: each first in worship is most highly favoured.
days.s: In a hymn calling for the Asvins to be worshipped first, at daybreak, the verse presses the point; Sāyaṇa, on 5.77.2, reads the evening clause as saying the gods do not accept an evening offering, since scripture gives them the forenoon.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.77.2, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 209188 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 5.82 to 6.3
days.key: None, verily, hath ever let or hindered this the most wise God’s mighty deed of magic, Whereby with all their flood, the lucid rivers fill not one sea wherein they pour their waters.
days.s: Before the hymn to Varuna turns to pleas for pardon, the singer marvels at the sea; Sāyaṇa, on 5.85.6, takes the magic as wisdom, and the deed as fitly Varuna’s, since the Supreme Lord abides in the forms of Varuna and the other gods.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 5.85.6, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 209192 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 6.4 to 6.14
days.key: I know not either warp or woof, I know not the web they weave when moving to the contest.
days.s: Praising Agni Vaisvanara, the singer owns an ignorance the next verse sets against the god’s knowledge; Sāyaṇa, on 6.9.2, explains the web as the sacrifice, the metres its warp and the Adhvaryu’s formulas its woof, or, for the knowers of the Self, as creation.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 6.9.2, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 209204 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 6.15 to 6.18
days.key: For true, I deem, thy strength is, thine the Mighty, thine, O Most Potent, thine the Conquering Victor; Strong, of the strong, Most Mighty, of the mighty, thine, driver of the churl to acts of bounty.
days.s: Praising Indra’s lone victories, the singer has just asked whether his great exploit is real; Sāyaṇa, on 6.18.3 and 4, hears a seer who doubted Indra’s power when he could not see him, and here settles that the power is there.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 6.18.3 and 6.18.4, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 186331 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 6.19 to 6.24
days.key: Mortals who yearn to worship ne’er dishonour, O Mighty God, thy Law who art Immortal.
days.s: Praising Indra, whose greatness passes earth and heaven, the hymn turns to his worshippers; Sāyaṇa, on 6.21.3, takes the Law as Indra’s abode in heaven and the gods there, and hears that those who would worship them never harm any living thing.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 6.21.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 310167 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 6.25 to 6.36
days.key: As rivers reach the sea, so, strong with praises, our holy songs reach him the Comprehensive.
days.s: Praising Indra, whom help, might and vigour attend like teams of horses, the singer turns to the songs; Sāyaṇa, on 6.36.3, reads the rivers as no longer seen apart once they enter the sea, and so every praise as becoming one with Indra.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 6.36.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 188373 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 6.37 to 6.45
days.key: Hard is thy love to win: thou art a Steer to him who longs for steers: Be to one craving steeds a Steed.
days.s: Near the end of a long hymn to Indra, among songs likened to cows lowing for their calves, the singer turns to his friendship; Sāyaṇa, on 6.45.26, takes that friendship as one that cannot be destroyed, and the ‘Steer’ as the giver of cattle.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 6.45.26, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 273533 (2020)

days.label: Rig Veda 6.46 to 6.49
days.key: Indra moves multiform by his illusions; for his Bay Steeds are yoked, ten times a hundred.
days.s: After verses on Indra raising the last and dropping old friends, the hymn turns to his many forms; Sāyaṇa, on 6.47.18, takes the ‘illusions’ as Indra’s knowledge and resolves, by which he assumes many bodies to reach many worshippers at once.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 6.47.18, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 338253 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 6.50 to 6.58
days.key: Mighty is homage: I adopt and use it. Homage hath held in place the earth and heaven.
days.s: After a plea not to suffer for another’s sin, the hymn to the Universal Gods praises reverence itself; Sāyaṇa, on 6.51.8, reads homage as mightiest because all is won by it, and heaven and earth as lasting long because creatures revere them.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 6.51.8, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 200162 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 6.59 to 6.66
days.key: As the birds fly forth from their resting places, so men with store of food rise at thy dawning.
days.s: Closing a hymn to the Dawn that praises her easy paths over hills and waters, the singer turns to the stir of morning; Sāyaṇa, on 6.64.6, reads the men who rise as those who share the offerings, or as those who earn their food.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 6.64.6, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 200403 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 6.67 to 6.75
days.key: Ye Twain have conquered, ne’er have you been conquered: never hath either of the Twain been vanquished. Ye, Indra-Visnu, when ye fought the battle, produced this infinite with three divisions.
days.s: Closing a hymn that calls Indra and Visnu to the Soma, the verse turns to their battle; Sāyaṇa, on 6.69.8, takes the ‘three divisions’ as worlds, Vedas and speech, an unmeasured whole the two contended for with the Asuras and strode across.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, commentary on 6.69.8, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ६.६९, revision 200457 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 7.1 to 7.7
days.key: THE men from fire-sticks, with their hands’ swift movement, have, in deep thought, engendered glorious Agni, Far-seen, with pointed flame, Lord of the homestead.
days.s: Opening a hymn asking Agni for wealth and sons, the verse tells of his kindling; Yāska, Nirukta 5.10, takes the ‘deep thought’ as the fingers, employed in actions, and the fire-sticks as named for the fire resting in them or born of their rubbing.
days.src: Yāska, Nirukta 5.10, in Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta, translation pp. 78 to 79, archive.org nighantuniruktao00yask (1921)

days.label: Rig Veda 7.8 to 7.18
days.key: E’en with the weak he wrought this matchless exploit: e’en with a goat he did to death a lion. He pared the pillar’s angles with a needle.
days.s: Late in a hymn on Indra’s aid to Sudas in battle, the verse names three marvels; Sāyaṇa, on 7.18.17, takes the weak one as Sudas when poor, and holds the three deeds not to be doubted as impossible, since Indra’s greatness surpasses them.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, commentary on 7.18.17, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ७.१८, revision 189176 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 7.19 to 7.28
days.key: None among men knows his own life’s duration: bear us in safety over these our troubles.
days.s: In a battle hymn to Indra, after a cry goes up to the gods for strength, the singer turns to the span of a life; Sāyaṇa, on 7.23.2, takes the ‘troubles’ as all the sins through which a life wastes away.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, commentary on 7.23.2, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ७.२३, revision 400689 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 7.29 to 7.34
days.key: Three fertilize the worlds with genial moisture: three noble Creatures cast a light before them. Three that give warmth to all attend the morning. All these have they discovered, these Vasisthas.
days.s: In a hymn on the Vasisthas and their birth, the verse credits them with a threefold lore; Sāyaṇa, on 7.33.7, citing the Śāṭyāyanaka, reads the triads as Agni, Vāyu and the Sun in earth, air and sky, and the Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, commentary on 7.33.7, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ७.३३, revision 327730 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 7.35 to 7.44
days.key: With offerings I propitiate the branches of this swift-moving God, the bounteous Visnu.
days.s: In a hymn where the assembly gathers to praise the gods and asks them for riches, the singer turns to Visnu; Sāyaṇa, on 7.40.5, takes Visnu as comprising all the gods, citing a Vedic text, and the other gods as though his branches.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, commentary on 7.40.5, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ७.४०, revision 224367 (2020)

days.label: Rig Veda 7.45 to 7.58
days.key: Maruts, accept this thousandfold allotment of household sacrifice and household treasure.
days.s: Midway through a long hymn to the Maruts, the singer turns from their splendour to their share of the home rite; Sāyaṇa, on 7.56.14, reads the single portion as a thousandfold, since an oblation spreads as far as the deity desires.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 7.56.14, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ७.५६, revision 403392 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 7.59 to 7.67
days.key: WHEN thou, O Sun, this day, arising sinless, shalt speak the truth to Varuna and Mitra, O Aditi, may all the Deities love us, and thou, O Aryaman, while we are singing.
days.s: A hymn chiefly to Mitra and Varuna opens on the rising Sun, watcher of mortal deeds; Sāyaṇa, on 7.60.1, reads ‘sinless’ as the word the Sun is asked to speak of the singers, so that among the gods they may truly be free of sin.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on 7.60.1, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ७.६०, revision 349701 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 7.68 to 7.78
days.key: WE have o’erpassed the limit of this darkness while, worshipping the Gods, we sang their praises.
days.s: At daybreak a hymn to the Asvins calls the twin gods to the rite; Sāyaṇa, on 7.73.1, reads the darkness crossed as ignorance with its effect, the sorrow of birth and death, or, since the rite is in hand, ignorance of how it is performed.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on 7.73.1, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ७.७३, revision 209146 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 7.79 to 7.89
days.key: Not our own will betrayed us, but seduction, thoughtlessness, Varuna wine, dice, or anger. The old is near to lead astray the younger: even sleep removeth not all evil-doing.
days.s: Told by the sages that Varuna is angry, the singer asks to be set free; Sāyaṇa, on 7.86.6, takes the cause of sin to be not a man’s own strength but fate fixed at birth, so the offence is one Varuna should forgive.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on 7.86.6, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ७.८६, revision 324074 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 7.90 to 7.100
days.key: What was there to be blamed in thee, O Visnu, when thou declaredst, I am Sipivista? Hide not this form from us, nor keep it secret, since thou didst wear another shape in battle.
days.s: Near the close of a hymn to Visnu that lauds his strides and his name, the verse returns to that name; Yāska, Nirukta 5.7 to 5.8, reads the name either as disparaging, with Aupamanyava, or as a name of praise, Visnu enveloped in rays.
days.src: Yāska, Nirukta 5.7 to 5.8, Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta (1920 to 1921), archive.org nighantuniruktao00yask

days.label: Rig Veda 7.101 to 8.1
days.key: When one of these repeats the other’s language, as he who learns the lesson of the teacher, Your every limb seems to be growing larger as ye converse with eloquence on the waters.
days.s: Hailing the frogs whose voices greet the first rains, the hymn turns to address them directly; Sāyaṇa, on 7.103.5, reads the growing limbs as bodies made truly whole: turned to clay in the hot season, the frogs come forth entire when rain falls.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on 7.103.5, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ७.१०३, revision 400502 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.2 to 8.4
days.key: The Gods seek him who presses out the Soma; they desire not sleep They punish sloth unweariedly.
days.s: Amid the Kanvas’ call to Indra, the hymn turns to the gods and the worshipper; Sāyaṇa, on 8.2.18, reads it as the gods, wishing to guard the presser, keeping him ever awake, and takes the word rendered ‘sloth’ as the gladdening Soma they tirelessly reach.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.2.18, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.२, revision 302478 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.5 to 8.7
days.key: There where the mountains downward slope, there by the meeting of the streams The Sage was manifest with song.
days.s: Amid long praise of Indra’s might, the hymn tells where a sage appears; Sāyaṇa, on 8.6.28, takes the sage as Indra, manifest through the rite or praise offered among hills and river meetings, and infers that the singers too worship in such places.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.6.28, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.६, revision 314241 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.8 to 8.12
days.key: Three places of the Asvins, erst concealed, are made apparent now.
days.s: Closing a long summons of the Asvins to the Kanvas’ Soma, the hymn turns to their approach; Sāyaṇa, on 8.8.23, takes the three places as the three wheels of their chariot, hidden until now, citing another hymn for its three wheels.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.8.23, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.८, revision 208919 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.13 to 8.18
days.key: And as we human beings, O Adityas, are akin to death, Graciously lengthen ye our lives that we may live.
days.s: Ending a hymn asking the Adityas for shelter and release from sin, the singers plead for life; Sāyaṇa, on 8.18.22, takes kinship with death as kinship with Yama, their death being near, and reads the plea as for long continuance in life.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.18.22, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.१८, revision 327230 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.19 to 8.22
days.key: Like a son cherished in his father’s house, Let our oblation rise unto the Gods.
days.s: After the singer imagines trading places with Agni, the hymn returns to the offering; Sāyaṇa, on 8.19.27, takes the cherished son as Agni, fed with offerings like a son by his father, who carries the oblation to the gods from the house of sacrifice.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.19.27, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.१९, revision 402086 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.23 to 8.26
days.key: Pathfinders even better than the eye, with unobstructed sight, Even when they close their lids, observant, they perceive.
days.s: Praising Mitra and Varuna, who look down from the sky, the hymn turns to their sight; Sāyaṇa, on 8.25.9, takes the closing of lids as their waking every creature to its work, their gaze a mild light pervading day and night.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.25.9, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.२५, revision 201711 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.27 to 8.33
days.key: Excellent Savitar hath mounted up on high for you, ye sure and careful Guides. Bipeds and quadrupeds, with several hopes and aims, and birds have settled to their tasks.
days.s: A hymn to all the gods, seeking their gifts at dawn, noon and dusk, here greets the rising sun; Sāyaṇa, on 8.27.12, reads the creatures’ tasks as some men performing the Agnihotra, others praising the gods, and beasts roaming to graze.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.27.12, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.२७, revision 208927 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.34 to 8.40
days.key: Agni bestows all vital power even as each man supplicates. He brings the Vasus strengthening gifts, and grants delight, in rest and stir, for every calling on the Gods.
days.s: Fourth in a hymn to Agni, the verse turns from his office as the worshipper’s messenger to his gifts; Sāyaṇa, on 8.39.4, reads the delight as happiness born of calm and of sense contact, and takes Agni as doing all, whatever god is invoked.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.39.4, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.३९, revision 275528 (2020)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.41 to 8.45
days.key: Sharpen this song of him who strives his utmost, sharpen, God Varuna, his strength and insight; May we ascend the ship that bears us safely, whereby we may pass over all misfortune.
days.s: The last of three verses to Varuna, who propped the heavens, prays for the singer before the hymn turns to the Asvins; Sāyaṇa, on 8.42.3, reads the ship as the sacrifice, the means of crossing the sea of suffering.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.42.3, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.४२, revision 208930 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.46 to 8.49
days.key: We have drunk Soma and become immortal; we have attained the light, the Gods discovered.
days.s: In a hymn on Soma at work within the drinker’s heart and limbs, the singers speak after the draught goes down; Sāyaṇa, on 8.48.3, takes the deathlessness as hoped for from drinking one who is himself deathless, and the light as shining heaven.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.48.3, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.४८, revision 202962 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.50 to 8.56
days.key: Let not this fetter bind us fast: may he release us for success; For strong is Indra and renowned.
days.s: In a hymn to the Adityas and Aditi, pleading for life and release, the verse turns for once to Indra; Sāyaṇa, on 8.56.8, reads the fetter as a binding net and Indra, controller of all, as keeping the speakers clear of it.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.56.8 (standard 8.67.8), sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.६७, revision 299570 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.57 to 8.62
days.key: The seven milk a single cow; the two set other five to work, On the stream’s loud-resounding bank.
days.s: Midway through a hymn to Agni, the verse speaks in numbers; Sāyaṇa, on 8.61.7, reads the seven as priests milking the one gharma of the hot-milk rite, and two of them, the adhvaryu priests, as directing five others, the sacrificer among them.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.61.7 (standard 8.72.7), sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.७२, revision 340872 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.63 to 8.74
days.key: All that is bare he covers o’er, all that is sick he medicines; The blind man sees, the cripple walks.
days.s: Early in a hymn to Soma, before prayers against enmity, the verse lists what he mends; Sāyaṇa, on 8.68.2, reads the covering as fruit for what lies fruitless, or as cloth he brings forth, and the healing as given through the sacrifice and as medicine.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.68.2 (standard 8.79.2), sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.७९, revision 202004 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.75 to 8.82
days.key: About the holy Law toils Savitar the God the horn of holy Law hath he spread far and wide. The holy Law hath quelled even mighty men of war.
days.s: In a hymn begging the Asvins to keep their friendship, the last verse turns to Savitar; Sāyaṇa, on 8.75.5, reads ‘holy Law’ as truth, by which Savitar quiets his rays at evening, and which by itself overcomes even an enemy’s great strength.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.75.5 (standard 8.86.5), sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.८६, revision 209020 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.83 to 8.89
days.key: One and another say, There is no Indra. Who hath beheld him? Whom then shall we honour?
days.s: Urging a truthful hymn, the singer reports a doubt that Indra himself answers next; Sāyaṇa, on 8.89.3, takes the doubter as the seer Nema of the Bhṛgu line, for whom, since no one has seen Indra, talk of him is mere words.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.89.3 (standard 8.100.3), sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.१००, revision 402088 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.90 to 8.96
days.key: When he enkindles Agni, man should with his heart attend the song: I with the priests have kindled him.
days.s: Closing a hymn in which a seer without cow or axe asks Agni to accept any fuel, the verse turns to the kindler; Sāyaṇa, on 8.91.22, reads the heart as a mind of faith and the song as the rite, attended in its season.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.91.22 (standard 8.102.22), sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.१०२, revision 321403 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 8.97 to 9.7
days.key: By means of this eternal fleece may Surya’s Daughter purify Thy Soma that is foaming forth.
days.s: Opening the book of hymns to Soma, a short hymn follows the juice from the press through the strainer to the milk; Sāyaṇa, on 9.1.6, takes the Sun’s daughter as the goddess Faith, citing the Vājasaneyins, for whom Faith purifies Soma.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 9.1.6, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ९.१, revision 339335 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 9.8 to 9.23
days.key: The Sun with his dear eye beholds that quarter of the heavens which priests Have placed within the sacred cell.
days.s: A hymn of rushing drops and seated priests closes here; Sāyaṇa, on 9.10.9, takes the beholder not as the sun but as Indra, and the ‘sacred cell’ as the heart, where he sees the Soma even after it is drunk.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 9.10.9, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ९.१०, revision 360656 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 9.24 to 9.45
days.key: Shedding the ancient fluid he is poured into the cleansing sieve: He, thundering, hath produced the Gods.
days.s: The hymn opens with Soma engendering the sun and the lights of heaven, and follows the juice as it is purified; Sāyaṇa, on 9.42.4, reads his begetting the gods as figurative, since wherever Soma is pressed, there the gods invariably appear.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 9.42.4, Sanskrit Wikisource, revision 310169 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 9.46 to 9.62
days.key: We have accepted thousands from Dhvasra’s and Purusanti’s hands: Swift runs this giver of delight.
days.s: Near a Soma hymn’s close, the singers turn to gifts received; Sāyaṇa, on 9.58.3, takes the givers as kings and cites the Śāṭyāyanaka, where two seers, feeling like swallowers of poison at so much, saw this hymn, and their wealth counted as taken, not accepted.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 9.58.3, Sanskrit Wikisource, revision 403221 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 9.63 to 9.66
days.key: O’er all thou rulest with these Two which, Soma Pavamana, stand, Turned, as thy stations, hitherward.
days.s: After Soma is hailed as a friend besought by friends, the singer turns to his rule; Sāyaṇa, on 9.66.2, reads the Two as the waxing and waning fortnights, when Soma the creeper gains and loses leaf by leaf and the gods drink his portions.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 9.66.2, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ९.६६, revision 315685 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 9.67 to 9.72
days.key: The man who reads the essence stored by saints, the Pavamani hymns, Tastes food completely purified, made sweet by Matarisvan’s touch.
days.s: After prayers to be made pure, the hymn’s last two verses turn to whoever studies these hymns; Sāyaṇa, on 9.67.31, reads the essence as the heart of the Veda gathered by the seers, and the food as sinless, first sweetened by the pure wind.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 9.67.31, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 363110 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 9.73 to 9.84
days.key: The raw, whose mass hath not been heated gains not this: they only which are dressed, which bear, attain to it.
days.s: Opening a hymn that hails Brahmanaspati’s filter, the verse sets the raw against the dressed; Sāyaṇa, on 9.83.1, reads the raw as one whose body no milk vow or like observance has heated, and the dressed who bear as the ripened, carrying the sacrifice through.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 9.83.1, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ९.८३, revision 322742 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 9.85 to 9.87
days.key: He glideth like a serpent from his ancient skin, and like a playful horse the Tawny Steer hath run.
days.s: Near the end of a long hymn, singers are bidden to praise Soma as he flows; Sāyaṇa, on 9.86.44, reads the old skin as the one Soma sheds in the pressing, and the gliding as his stream slipping out through the filter.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 9.86.44, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ९.८६, revision 324716 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 9.88 to 9.96
days.key: Father of holy hymns, Soma flows onward the Father of the earth, Father of heaven: Father of Agni, Surya’s generator, the Father who begat Indra and Visnu.
days.s: After a shared prayer for welfare, the hymn turns to Soma’s titles; Sāyaṇa, on 9.96.5, reads all this begetting as coming to pass at the pressing, since Soma strengthens the gods, and Indra’s begetting as the gladness he stirs when drunk.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 9.96.5, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ९.९६, revision 307921 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 9.97 to 9.99
days.key: Part, like a knotted tangle, while they cleanse thee, O Soma, righteous and unrighteous conduct.
days.s: After asking Soma to set the winds free like unbraided hair, the singer asks a second untying; Sāyaṇa, on 9.97.18, hears a plea that the singer, bound by sins, be untied from them like a knot, and given a straight path and strength.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 9.97.18, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ९.९७, revision 402120 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 9.100 to 9.107
days.key: Close to thy bosom am I, Soma, day and night. O Tawny-hued, for friendship sake. Surya himself refulgent with his glow have we o’ertaken in his course like birds.
days.s: After a plea against the fiends that beset him, the singer speaks of his closeness to Soma; Sāyaṇa, on 9.107.20, takes the blazing sun as Soma himself in the highest place, whom the singers fly up to reach, as birds fly beyond the sun.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 9.107.20, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 400618 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 9.108 to 10.3
days.key: When we most ignorant neglect the statutes of you, O Deities with whom is knowledge, Wise Agni shall correct our faults and failings, skilled to assign each God his fitting season.
days.s: In a hymn asking Agni to worship the gods in season, the singers own their lapses; Sāyaṇa, on 10.2.4, takes Agni as Sviṣṭakṛt, maker of the well-offered rite, who knows what was neglected and fills up each rite with its fruit.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.2.4, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 343045 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.4 to 10.11
days.key: Agni I deem my Kinsman and my Father, count him my Brother and my Friend for ever. I honour as the face of lofty Agni in heaven the bright and holy light of Surya.
days.s: Asking Agni to bless the rite, the singer says what the god is to him; Sāyaṇa, on 10.7.3, reads the second line as a likeness: the singer tends the Āhavanīya fire, Agni’s face, as someone worships the sun’s bright disc to gain a wish.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.7.3, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 207987 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.12 to 10.17
days.key: The Sun receive thine eye, the Wind thy spirit; go, as thy merit is, to earth or heaven.
days.s: At the pyre, having asked Agni to bear the dead to the Fathers, the singer turns to the dead man; Sāyaṇa, on 10.16.3, takes the spirit as the breath, going to the outer wind, and merit as good deeds, whose fruit he goes to enjoy.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.16.3, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 333348 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.18 to 10.26
days.key: As the days follow days in close succession, as with the seasons duly come the seasons, As each successor fails not his foregoer, so form the lives of these, O great Ordainer.
days.s: In a hymn that sends Death away from the living, the singer turns to the Ordainer; Sāyaṇa, on 10.18.5, takes the successor who does not forsake his foregoer as a son who does not leave his father by dying first.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.18.5, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 353436 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.27 to 10.31
days.key: A man should think on wealth and strive to win it by adoration on the path of Order, Counsel himself with his own mental insight, and grasp still nobler vigour with his spirit.
days.s: After a prayer to pass beyond all troubles, the hymn to all the gods turns to a man’s duties; Sāyaṇa, on 10.31.2, takes the counsel as meditating on the gods at the offering, and the nobler vigour as the all-pervading self, grasped in meditation.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.31.2, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 202075 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.32 to 10.37
days.key: “Play not with dice, [but] cultivate your corn-land. Enjoy the gain, and deem that wealth sufficient. There are your cattle, there your wife, O gambler”: So this good Savitr himself has told me.
days.s: Near the close of a gambler’s lament for the wife and home his dice have cost him, counsel comes from a god; Sāyaṇa, on 10.34.13, reads the counsel as the secret of dharma, declared by Savitṛ, maker of revealed and remembered teaching.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.34.13, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं १०.३४, revision 206574 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.38 to 10.44
days.key: Far went our earliest invocation of the Gods, and won us glories that can never be surpassed. They who could not ascend the ship of sacrifice, sink down in desolation, trembling with alarm.
days.s: Between bidding Indra sit on the holy grass and wishing the evil-hearted far away, the singer sets two fates at the sacrifice side by side; Sāyaṇa, on 10.44.6, reads those left behind as evildoers without Indra’s grace, brought low by debt, and Yāska, Nirukta 5.25, as those who stayed in this very world, or in debt.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.44.6, sa.wikisource revision 328215 (2021); Yāska, Nirukta 5.25, in Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta (1921)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.45 to 10.51
days.key: Agni, we know thy three powers in three stations, we know thy forms in many a place divided. We know what name supreme thou hast in secret: we know the source from which thou hast proceeded.
days.s: After a verse on Agni’s three births, the singer claims to know the god whole; Sāyaṇa, on 10.45.2, reads the three as fire, wind and sun, the many places as the sacrificial fires, and the secret name as hidden from those without the Veda.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.45.2, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं १०.४५, revision 296628 (2020)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.52 to 10.60
days.key: HERE is one light for thee, another yonder: enter the third and he therewith united. Uniting with a body be thou welcome, dear to the Gods in their sublimest birthplace.
days.s: Opening a hymn that speaks to Vajin and praises the Fathers, the verse offers him three lights; Sāyaṇa, on 10.56.1, hears a father speaking to his dead son, and reads the lights as fire, wind and sun, for his warmth, breath and self to join.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.56.1, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं १०.५६, revision 321754 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.61 to 10.64
days.key: Wise Deities, who have dominion o’er the world, ye thinkers over all that moves not and that moves, Save us from uncommitted and committed sin, preserve us from all sin to-day for happiness.
days.s: In a hymn asking the All-Gods and Adityas, stanza after stanza, for happiness, the singer seeks release from wrongdoing; Sāyaṇa, on 10.63.8, reads ‘committed’ sin as the body’s and ‘uncommitted’ as the mind’s, done by no hand or foot.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.63.8, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं १०.६३, revision 275531 (2020)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.65 to 10.70
days.key: Like a dark steed adorned with pearl, the Fathers have decorated heaven With constellations. They set the light in day, in night the darkness. Brhaspati cleft the rock and found the cattle.
days.s: Near the close of a hymn on Bṛhaspati winning the cows from Vala, the singer looks to the night sky; Sāyaṇa, on 10.68.11, reads ‘the Fathers’ as the guarding gods, who lit heaven with the lunar mansions when Bṛhaspati broke the rock.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.68.11, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं १०.६८, revision 314349 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.71 to 10.79
days.key: He wanders on in profitless illusion: the Voice he heard yields neither fruit, nor blossom.
days.s: Setting those to whom Vak unveils herself against those who only hear her, the hymn turns to one who hears in vain; Yāska, Nirukta 1.20, reads fruit and flower as the meaning of speech, and the illusion as a semblance of speech.
days.src: Yāska, Nirukta 1.20, in Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta, archive.org nighantuniruktao00yask (1921)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.80 to 10.85
days.key: Ye will not find him who produced these creatures: another thing hath risen up among you. Enwrapt in misty cloud, with lips that stammer, hymn-chanters wander and are discontented.
days.s: Closing the second hymn to Visvakarman, the verse turns to its hearers; Sāyaṇa, on 10.82.7, reads the mist as ignorance veiling the supreme Lord, whose reality is other than the individual self, and the chanters as seeking only enjoyment here and hereafter.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.82.7, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 353423 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.86 to 10.89
days.key: I have heard mention of two several pathways, ways of the Fathers and of Gods and mortals. On these two paths each moving creature travels, each thing between the Father and the Mother.
days.s: In a hymn to Agni Vaisvanara as fire and Sun, the singer turns to two roads; Sāyaṇa, on 10.88.15, reads them as the gods’ way and the fathers’ way, by which all between heaven and earth, hallowed by fire, goes to those worlds.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.88.15, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 363752 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.90 to 10.94
days.key: So mighty is his greatness; yea, greater than this is Purusa. All creatures are one-fourth of him, three-fourths eternal life in heaven.
days.s: Having called Purusa all that was and will be, the hymn measures him; Sāyaṇa, on 10.90.3, reads the world, past, present and to come, as his greatness, not his true nature, and the quarter as marking it small beside Brahman, which has no measure.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.90.3, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 336240 (2022)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.95 to 10.99
days.key: With Soma as their Sovran Lord the Plants hold colloquy and say: O King, we save from death the man whose cure a Brahman undertakes.
days.s: Near the close of a hymn in which a healer calls on the Plants to free his patient, the Plants themselves speak; Sāyaṇa, on 10.97.22, takes the Brahman as a physician who knows the power of herbs, and the one saved as his patient.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.97.22, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 317292 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.100 to 10.106
days.key: Make pleasant hymns, spin out your songs and praises: build ye a ship equipped with oars for transport. Prepare the implements, make all things ready, and let the sacrifice, my friends, go forward.
days.s: Calling friends to wake and kindle Agni, the hymn sets them working like farmers; Sāyaṇa, on 10.101.2, takes the ship as the piling of the fire altar, carried through by ploughing as by an oar, and the implements as ploughs and yokes.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.101.2, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 368305 (2023)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.107 to 10.114
days.key: The liberal die not, never are they ruined: the liberal suffer neither harm nor trouble.
days.s: Praising the sacrificial Guerdon and those who give it, the hymn names their reward; Sāyaṇa, on 10.107.8, takes the liberal as those who feed others by giving wealth, and their not dying as their attaining the state of gods.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.107.8, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 208417 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.115 to 10.123
days.key: IN the beginning rose Hiranyagarbha, born Only Lord of all created beings. He fixed and holdeth up this earth and heaven. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
days.s: The verse opens a hymn whose verses, all but the last, end on one question; Sāyaṇa, on 10.121.1, takes ‘What’ as pointing to Prajapati, whose nature is not known, or as his name Ka, since he desires to create, or since he is happiness.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.121.1, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 400427 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.124 to 10.133
days.key: That One Thing, breathless, breathed by its own nature: apart from it was nothing whatsoever.
days.s: In a hymn on the time when neither non-existent nor existent was, which asks whence creation came, the verse tells what alone there was; Sāyaṇa, on 10.129.2, takes the One as Brahman, known throughout the Vedānta, and ‘its own nature’ as māyā, undivided from it.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 10.129.2, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 402226 (2024)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.134 to 10.147
days.key: The Munis, girdled with the wind, wear garments soiled of yellow hue. They, following the wind’s swift course go where the Gods have gone before.
days.s: After the long-haired one who upholds heaven and earth, the hymn turns to the Munis; Sāyaṇa, on 10.136.2, takes them as sons of Vātaraśana, seers of things beyond sense, clad in soiled bark, who by worship of breath attain the wind’s own state.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 10.136.2, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 319729 (2021)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.148 to 10.165
days.key: By Faith is Agni kindled, through Faith is oblation offered up. We celebrate with praises Faith upon the height of happiness.
days.s: Opening a hymn that calls on Faith at dawn, noon and sunset, the verse honours her in the rite; Sāyaṇa, on 10.151.1, takes faith as a particular longing in a person, who lights the fires only when an exceeding regard for them arises in him.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 10.151.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 208435 (2019)

days.label: Rig Veda 10.166 to 10.191
days.key: FROM Fervour kindled to its height Eternal Law and Truth were born: Thence was the Night produced, and thence the billowy flood of sea arose.
days.s: The verse opens a hymn of origins ending with the Creator forming sun, moon, heaven and earth; Sāyaṇa, on 10.190.1, takes ‘Law’ as true intention and ‘Truth’ as true speech, born of fervour spent for creation, which he explains as contemplating what would be made.
days.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 10.190.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 340861 (2022)
